explanation: Use two pointers on the already sorted array. Increase the left pointer when the sum is too small and decrease the right pointer when it is too large. Allow the pointers to coincide because this EPI contract permits reusing one element.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: With sorted values, a sum below target rules out the current left value paired with any value at or below right, so left can advance safely. A sum above target symmetrically rules out the current right value. The inclusive left ≤ right condition retains same-index pairs, which this EPI problem explicitly permits. If the pointers cross, all candidate pairs have been excluded.
walkthrough: For sorted [-8, 1, 6, 13] and target 12, begin with -8 + 13 = 5 and advance left. Next 1 + 13 = 14, so move right to 6. Then 1 + 6 = 7, so move left to that same 6. Now 6 + 6 = 12; reusing the element is allowed, so return true.
edgeCases: A single value can satisfy the target by being used twice.
The long sum protects against overflow when input values are near signed-int limits.
